data.narrative:
Biofire is a Series A-stage defense and security company founded by Kai Kloepfer that has raised $52.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms—all operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression valuation, using the $52.9M raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, implies a valuation of $106M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Castelion ($1.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—yields a median valuation of $700M, with a full range spanning $125M to $4.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business model maturity and market traction within the defense tech space.

Triangulating these two methods produces a defensible range of $90M (low) to $805M (high), with a median estimate of $403M. The substantial gap between methods reflects uncertainty around whether Biofire's traction more closely tracks the stage-defined capital progression or the upper-quartile peer benchmarks. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, regulatory pathway clarity, and revenue trajectory relative to the peer set. Near-term funding dynamics and customer wins will be critical inputs for range refinement.
